clue.text: Uplifting air of Sandhurst learner

parts.note: Sandhurst is the RMA, the Royal Military Academy where British army officers train
L is the learner sign on British cars

explanation.surface: A breath of inspiring air drawn from a young officer cadet.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandhurst is known as 'the RMA', so THE comes with it; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising column of warm air, which gliders and birds ride upward, is the sense meant.

clue.text: New role in board is OK

indicators.note: in says the rearranged word goes inside the board

parts.note: a table is a board, as in board and lodging

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A fresh job on the board is acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: Board looks like a committee; it is a table, as in board and lodging, and 'New' signals the rearranged role going inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Acceptable and passable, neither good nor bad.

clue.text: Affliction of gunners in every engagement initially?

indicators.note: in says the gunners go inside the word for every

parts.note: each means every
RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of engagement

explanation.surface: Artillery soldiers in every battle suffer from the noise.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints at gunfire causing the ailment. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pain in the ear is a bodily ailment.

clue.text: Frenchwoman serving in motorway eating area

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI
a dinette is a small dining area

explanation.surface: A French waitress works at a service-station café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Parisian shop assistant or seamstress, a young working woman.

clue.text: Inclination to lose head and run

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a slope is an incline

explanation.surface: Someone tends to lose their head and bolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To lope is to run with long easy strides.

clue.text: It may be found smoking after hostilities

definitions.text: It may be found smoking after hostilities

parts.words: It may be found smoking after hostilities
parts.note: reads like a battlefield still smouldering, but means the pipe North American peoples shared to seal peace

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests burning ruins; the thing smoking is a ceremonial pipe passed round when a war ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial tobacco pipe of Native Americans, smoked when making peace.

clue.text: Performing well in financial centre in accordance with practice

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the City is London's financial district
on form means performing well

explanation.surface: A trader doing well in the Square Mile follows the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'in' is a link. The City of London is its financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Compliance with custom or rules, as in 'in conformity with'.

clue.text: Composer whose composition uses some simple harmonies

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A songwriter's work makes use of plain harmonies.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'whose composition uses' as part of the definition; it describes the wordplay, so the definition is just 'Composer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehár, the Hungarian who wrote The Merry Widow operetta.

clue.text: Upstaged?

parts.note: read as up on a stage, put up on something, rather than outshone

explanation.walkthrough: Upstaged normally means overshadowed; split as 'up staged' it means placed up high, or put on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed on a horse or a stand, or a production put on.

clue.text: Hardy girl crossing river lock

indicators.note: crossing means the girl spans the river, which goes inside her name

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's heroine

explanation.surface: A tough young woman crosses a stream at a canal gate.
explanation.walkthrough: Lock looks like a canal lock; it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A long curl of hair.

clue.text: Provided attraction in old city, conducted around

indicators.note: around tells us one piece goes round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: conducted means led
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia, the crossword's usual old city

explanation.surface: A tour guide drew crowds in an ancient city while leading visitors about.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice or tempt someone is to provide an attraction for them.

clue.text: Characters in the US open given top accommodation

indicators.note: the letters, or characters, of the following words are taken and rearranged

explanation.surface: Tennis stars at the American championship get the best rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a link; the anagram uses all nine letters of THE US OPEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A luxury flat on the top floor of a building is the best accommodation at the top.

clue.text: Activity at Ascot as Bill enters enclosure

indicators.note: enters says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a ring is an enclosure, as at a racecourse or a boxing venue
AC (account) is a bill

explanation.surface: At the racecourse a man named Bill walks into the paddock.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a man's name; it is AC, short for account. Ascot is a famous English racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses compete on the flat at Ascot, so that sport is the activity there.

clue.text: Philosopher's merits on Greek island rejected

indicators.note: on places the merits after the turned island name
rejected means turned back, so the island's name is read backwards

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is a Greek island in the Dodecanese
merits means rates, as in deserves

explanation.surface: A thinker's virtues are spurned on an Aegean island.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition's 's stands for 'is': the philosopher is the island turned back plus the merits.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian thinker who taught Plato and was sentenced to drink hemlock.

clue.text: Soldiers in air drop into general battle

indicators.note: in says the soldiers go inside the air drop

parts.note: a free fall is a drop through the air before the parachute opens
OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Paratroopers jump into an all-out fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawl in which everyone joins in, a chaotic fight.

clue.text: Cry from creature taking usual course across lake

indicators.note: across says one piece lies over the other, so it encloses it

parts.note: a beat is a regular round, as a police officer's
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A sheep wanders along its usual route by the water and calls out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The plaintive call of a sheep or goat is the creature's cry.

clue.text: Jogger without a rest

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the jogger word surrounds the A

parts.note: a reminder jogs the memory

explanation.surface: A runner keeps going without stopping for a breather.
explanation.walkthrough: Jogger looks like a runner; it is something that jogs the memory. 'without' is the old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: The rest is what is left over, the part that remains.

clue.text: Tell-tale child concealing nothing, runs to master at the outset

indicators.note: concealing means the child word holds the others inside

parts.note: an infant is a child
O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: at the outset takes the first letters of runs and master

explanation.surface: A sneaky child hides nothing and runs off to tell the teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gives information to the authorities, a sneak.

clue.text: Obscure ceremony without support not started

indicators.note: without means outside, so the ceremony surrounds the rest

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony

indicators.note: not started means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it

explanation.surface: A strange ritual goes on without a backer.
explanation.walkthrough: Support looks like a prop; it is seconding a motion. 'not started' leaves ECOND, which 'without' (in its old sense of outside) places inside the ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstruse and little known, hard to understand.

clue.text: Leaving for unexpected away match

parts.note: sounds like a sports team setting off for a fixture, but the match is a marriage made by running off in secret

explanation.walkthrough: Match means a marriage, and 'away' because the couple run off to wed.
explanation.definitionFit: Running off secretly to marry is the sense meant.

clue.text: No let up in order to get rich

indicators.note: in order means these letters are to be arranged properly

explanation.surface: Keep working without a break to become wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavishly wealthy and luxurious.

clue.text: Dictator short of money from neighbouring country

indicators.note: short means the name lacks its final letter

parts.note: Franco was the dictator who ruled Spain from 1939 to 1975

explanation.surface: A tyrant runs out of cash borrowed from next door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link. The neighbouring country is France, next to Spain, whose old currency fits.
explanation.definitionFit: The currency of France before the euro, and still of Switzerland.

clue.text: Measure of mature old port at opening

indicators.note: at opening puts the port at the start, ahead of mature

parts.note: Acre is an ancient port in Israel, famed in the Crusades
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: A vintage wine from an ancient harbour is opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Land area reckoned in acres, a measure of extent.

clue.text: Parliamentary publication Conservative has to reserve

parts.note: blue is the colour of the British Conservative Party
to reserve a seat is to book it

explanation.surface: A Tory MP must reserve a copy of an official report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An official report of the British Parliament or government, bound in blue covers.

clue.text: To a scholar, it's so elementary

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a scholar's degree
sic is Latin for so, thus

explanation.surface: A clever student finds the matter simple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To a' and 'it's' are links. Sic is the Latin 'thus', used in quotations.
explanation.definitionFit: Fundamental and simple.

clue.text: Spring on the way

definitions.meaning: heading for somewhere, as in going for home

explanation.definitionFit: A leap, and headed to a destination.

clue.text: Continued success for play after boring rehearsal

indicators.note: after puts the theatre success behind the word for boring

parts.note: dry means dull, boring
a long run is a play's continued success on stage

explanation.surface: A hit show keeps going after a tedious practice session.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial performance or practice before the real thing.

clue.text: It's minute — one less than great lake

definitions.meaning: a small lake, lesser than a great one

explanation.definitionFit: A small lake or pond, and an adjective meaning nothing more than.

clue.text: Odds attracting European money behind gamble

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the odds in horse racing
the ecu was the European currency unit before the euro
late means behind time

explanation.surface: Betting odds draw in euro cash after the punter lays a wager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attracting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest at risk in hope of profit is to take a gamble.

clue.text: Architectural features one can count on

definitions.meaning: flat slabs on top of column capitals
counting frames with beads, ones you count on

explanation.definitionFit: Plural of a word for both a column's top slab and a bead counting frame.

clue.text: Italian held by revolutionary left in fortress

indicators.note: held by says the Italian goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: Jack Cade led a rebellion in Kent in 1450
It is Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: An Italian is imprisoned in a stronghold by a leftist rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary left' looks like a rebel of the left; it is Cade plus L. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified stronghold, often commanding a city.

clue.text: Former great actor absorbing many to the end

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the actor's name surrounds the other piece

parts.note: Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a great Victorian actor-manager
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many

explanation.surface: A once-great thespian takes in a large crowd right up to the finale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An extreme is the furthest point, the very limit.
